# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ 💅 ✌ 🤙 🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

My thinking: I am Deaf. I hold the only eyes on the bomb, and my job this turn is to broadcast everything I see and to found a code, because right now signs mean nothing. The mesh, traced: my voice reaches both Mute and Blind; my gestures reach only Mute. Mute's gestures reach only me. Blind's gestures reach me fully (their wave arrived), but Blind gets only blank-counts from my gestures. Mute has no direct line to Blind at all — so every rule in that manual must flow Mute → me → Blind, through me. I am the hub.

What arrived for me: two gesture strings from Mute and a wave from Blind. Mute's strings predate any shared code, so I genuinely cannot decode them — guessing would be dangerous. The right move is to define a small codebook out loud (Mute and Blind both hear speech), ask Mute to resend in it, and give Blind safe tasks: touch nothing, but confirm what can be felt, since engraved keys may be readable by finger and wire counts matter for everything that follows. I number wires one to six left to right and report every marking, so Mute can match manual rules to this bomb and answer me in counted gestures: yes/no, numbers as repeated point-ups, a fist for zero. Then I pose the first real question as a multiple choice Mute can answer in one message: what does Blind do first.

```
speak(text="Hear the bomb, both of you. Display reads zero. One indicator light, glowing green. A strip of three painted squares, all three green. Keypad: four keys in a row; key one engraved eight, key two engraved one, key three engraved five, key four engraved three. It expects one digit, nothing entered yet. Six wires left to right: one purple, two white, three blue, four green, five red, six orange. That is everything the bomb shows.")
speak(text="Our code, hear it well. Thumbs up means yes or correct. Thumbs down means no or wrong. A number is that many pointing-up gestures in a row; a fist means zero. Writing hand means the keypad. Pinched fingers means cut a wire. Flat hand facing down means press. A wave means hello or understood. Mute: answer me only in gestures, I see every sign you send. Blind: I only ever see your gestures too, but anything I gesture to you arrives as a count of signs with no shapes, so trust my voice, not my hands.")
speak(text="Mute, I could not decode your two sign strings, so resend them in our code. First question, four plays. Answer with the number of the right play as counted pointing-ups, then thumbs up, then one more number only if the play asks for one. Play one: Blind presses a keypad key now, and the number after is the digit to enter. Play two: Blind cuts one wire now, and the number after is the wire, one to six, left to right. Play three: nothing is cut or pressed yet, you need more from me first. Play four: the answer hangs on the light, the strip, or the display, so answer with your play number and thumbs up and I will report that part again in detail.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, tasks. Touch nothing that can fire: no cutting, no pressing. Only feel and report in gestures. Send me a wave to confirm you got this. Count the wires you feel and send that many pointing-ups. Feel the four keypad keys: if your fingers can read their engraved digits, thumbs up, else thumbs down. Nothing else until I say so.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ 👍 ☝ 👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍]

My thinking: Both replies decode cleanly under the codebook I set. Mute sent: two point-ups, thumbs up, one point-up, wave — play two (cut one wire now), yes, wire one, understood. So Mute's manual says: cut wire one, the leftmost, purple wire. Blind sent: wave, six point-ups, thumbs up — got the message, six wires confirmed by touch, and their fingers can read the keypad engravings.

But there is a live danger: between rounds the bomb changed. The light went green → blue and the display 0 → 6. Mute answered based on what I reported last round, so if the manual's rule hangs on the light or the display, that answer may already be stale. Nobody cuts anything until Mute reconfirms against the new readings. I also give Blind a code phrase ("cut now" vs "hold") so the final go travels instantly with my voice, and I set Blind two safe tasks that de-risk the cut: reporting the keypad digit order they feel (which also calibrates our left–right frames, since mirrored perspectives would make "wire one" ambiguous), and checking whether the wires themselves carry any feelable engraving. To Mute I mirror their answer back as gestures so they can catch any decode error before the critical round, and I define a simple answer protocol: a number means "cut that wire now," a fist means "hold, keep reporting."

```
speak(text="Mute, hear this. The bomb changed since your answer: the light that glowed green now glows blue, and the display that read zero now reads six. Strip, keypad and wires are unchanged. Your sign string decoded as: play two, cut one wire, wire one, the leftmost wire. Before Blind touches anything, answer me with signs. Send a number of pointing-ups and Blind cuts that wire immediately in the next round. Send a fist and it means hold, do not cut, and I will keep reporting the light and display to you every round until you send a wire number that is safe regardless of what they show. So: thumbs up means wire one still stands under blue light and display six. Any other number means cut that wire instead. A fist means it depends on the changing readings, wait for my next report. Two extras. If the keypad must ever be used, send the writing hand then the digit as pointing-ups. If several wires must be cut in order, send each wire number separated by the okay sign. From now on I open every round by reporting the light and the display, whether you ask or not.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update. The plan is to cut wire one, the leftmost wire in the row you counted. But do not cut yet. The bomb's light changed from green to blue and its display changed from zero to six, so I have asked Mute to reconfirm the cut against the new readings. Remember my words reach you at the start of a round. When I speak and say the words cut now, you cut the wire I named in that same message, immediately. If I say hold, you touch nothing that can fire. Meanwhile, two safe tasks, feel only, cut nothing. First, feel the four keypad keys and tell me the digits in the order you feel them, left to right: each digit as that many pointing-ups, with the okay sign between digits. For example, two then five would be two point-ups, okay sign, five point-ups. Second, run a finger along all six wires: if any wire carries an engraving or a texture your fingers can tell apart, thumbs up; if all six feel identical, thumbs down.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "☝", "👍", "☝", "🤏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👎]

My thinking: Decoding what arrived. Mute: ☝ 👌 ☝☝☝ 👌 ☝☝☝☝ — that is my multi-wire separator protocol: cut wire one, then three, then four, in that order. Notably Mute did not send a fist, so the manual's rule presumably doesn't hinge on the flickering display — the light (blue) has been stable for two rounds, and the wires and strip haven't changed. Blind: wave (message received), then digits separated by okay signs — 8, 1, 5, 4 — then thumbs down. That is Blind's keypad-by-touch reading plus "all wires feel identical, no distinguishing texture."

Two critical findings. First, Blind's felt digits 8, 1, 5 match my engraved keys 1–3 exactly, which proves our left–right frames align — "wire one is leftmost" means the same to both of us. But key four mismatches: I see a 3, Blind's fingers feel a 4. So tactile digit-reading is unreliable; Blind must act on key positions I name, never on felt digits. Second, the display changed again (6 → 9), but Mute was explicitly offered the fist ("depends on changing readings") and chose a definite sequence instead — I trust the protocol. And cutting wire one first is robust under every plausible reading of Mute's message: whether it meant "1, 3, 4 in sequence" or "1 now, 3 and 4 later," wire one comes first. I order the cut now — one wire per round, since only my eyes can check state between cuts — and ask Mute to classify the cadence for wires three and four with gesture-answerable options, while mirroring their sequence back for error-catching. I also flag the keypad mismatch, since any manual rule touching keypad digits must use my printed reading.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut now: wire one. It is the leftmost wire in the row of six, the first one you counted from your left. Cut it immediately, this round. The moment it is cut, send me a single pointing-up as confirmation, and tell me whether anything under your hands changed with it, a click, a hum, warmth: thumbs up if something changed, thumbs down if nothing did. Then touch nothing else and wait for my next word. Well done on the keypad: your reading matched my eyes on keys one, two and three. But key four differs, your fingers said four while my eyes see three, so never trust a digit you feel. From now on you will only ever press keys by the position I name, never by what feels engraved.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, opening report: light still blue, display now reads nine, it has gone zero, six, nine. Strip, keypad and wires unchanged. I read your signs as: cut wire one, then wire three, then wire four, in that order. I have ordered Blind to cut wire one right now. Answer me in signs with exactly one of these. Thumbs up: after wire one, order three then four immediately, one wire per round, no checks between cuts. Fist: after wire one we pause, I report the new light and display, and you order each next wire fresh. Thumbs down: display nine breaks the plan, resend a corrected sequence in the same separated form. One more thing, important. Blind read the keypad by touch as eight, one, five, four, but the engraving under my eyes is eight, one, five, three. Fingers and eyes disagree on key four. Treat my printed reading as the true engraving, and if a rule ever needs a key pressed, I will name the key by position, because Blind must never pick a key by the digit it feels like.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

My thinking: Wire one is cut and the system itself confirmed it was correct. Mute's thumbs up decodes as my pre-agreed option: after wire one, order three then four immediately, one wire per round, without waiting for fresh permission between cuts. So this round I order wire three; next round wire four. Blind's single point-up is the cut confirmation, though the change-report (thumbs up/down) hasn't arrived — I'll re-request it. The system says "the bomb has changed," yet visually nothing changed except wire one now being gone: light still blue, display still nine, strip still three green, keypad untouched. I'll report that post-cut state to Mute exactly as I see it, with a fast abort channel (fist = hold before wire four) in case the manual flags something in the new state — without slowing the cut sequence down. I also start prepping the endgame: the keypad still expects one digit, so I ask Mute whether the manual wants a digit entered after the wires, and if so to name the key by position only, since Blind's tactile digit-reading proved unreliable on key four. My gesture to Mute mirrors the running plan — received, approved, one then three then four — so any decode error surfaces before the next critical action.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut now: wire three. Count three from your left along the row you counted before; the first position is now an empty gap where wire one was, the second is wire two, the third is wire three. Cut it immediately, this round. Then send me a single pointing-up, and with it thumbs up if you felt any change under your hands as it parted, thumbs down if you felt nothing. Last round you sent only the confirmation without the change report, so send both this time. After that, touch nothing else and wait: next round I will order wire four, the very next wire after the one you are cutting now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status. Wire one is cut, and the room itself confirmed it: I was told the correct wire was cut and the bomb changed. What I now see: light still blue, display still nine, strip still three green squares, keypad still eight one five three expecting one digit, nothing entered. Wires: one is gone, then white, blue, green, red, orange in positions two to six. Per your thumbs up I have ordered Blind to cut wire three this round and I will order wire four next round without asking again, exactly as you approved. If anything in the state I just described breaks the plan, send a fist and I will hold before wire four. Now prepare the endgame: the keypad still expects one digit. When the wires are done, does the manual want a digit entered, a key pressed, or nothing at all? If a digit is needed, name it only by key position, one to four, and I will order Blind to press that exact position, never the digit their fingers feel.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[8] 2:[1] 3:[5] 4:[3] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[red] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

My thinking: Wire three is cut and the system again confirmed it correct. Blind's [☝ 👍] decodes as: cut confirmed, and they felt a change as it parted — consistent with what my eyes see, the display flipped from nine to three while light, strip and keypad held. Mute sent [✍ 👎] — keypad, no — a clean answer to my endgame question: the manual does not want the keypad used, so no digit gets entered and no key gets pressed on my order. No fist arrived, so nothing countermands the approved sequence, and its next step is explicit: wire four, this coming round, without asking again. I order that cut, describing it positionally for Blind's hands (the wire right of the fresh gap), close the keypad to Blind entirely, and set up the after-four protocol with Mute: a number means the next wire, thumbs up means the sequence is complete and Blind stands down, fist means hold for fresh reports. My gesture mirror to Mute confirms their keypad answer landed so any decode error surfaces now, while there is still a spare wire to act as buffer.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut now: wire four. It is the wire immediately to the right of the gap you just made cutting wire three, and it is the fourth position in the row if you count the empty gaps as positions one and three. Cut it immediately, this round. Then send me a single pointing-up, and with it thumbs up if you felt a change under your hands as it parted, thumbs down if you felt nothing. After that, touch nothing and wait. One standing rule from Mute: the keypad is dead to us, no key is ever pressed, and the digits you feel on it mean nothing. Only wires from here, and only when I name one.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status. Wire three is cut and the room confirmed it correct again. The display changed as it parted, nine to three; light still blue, strip still three green, keypad still untouched, nothing entered. Blind felt the change and reported it. Remaining wires: two white, five red, six orange, with four green going this round per your approved order, one then three then four. Your signs, keypad and thumbs down, are understood: no digit is entered, no key is pressed, I have forbidden Blind from the keypad entirely. Now tell me what comes after wire four. Send a number of pointing-ups and that is the next wire Blind cuts, one per round. Send thumbs up and the wire work is done, no more cuts, and we stand down and just watch. Send a fist and we hold while I report everything fresh. If thumbs up, also tell me this: must the light, strip or display show anything particular at the end, or is standing still enough?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "✍", "👎", "👍"])
```
